narratives.Overview:
1. Make first-class operator discovery of the existing explicit recovery: README and/or doctor cold-start recovery copy must name occupancy:release --session-id=<id from occupancy.json> (and that bare session:end without a presented identity refuses while the lease is live).
2. Keep TTL claim-over and the deny-embedded copy-paste recipe as existing mechanisms. Do not invent a new unlock verb whose sole job is to clear abandoned leases.
3. Reframe the defect around abandoned live sessionId plus normal-shell empty identity. Treat host:none / address:none as ordinary unset metadata, not the lock cause.
4. Do not reopen anonymous live auto-release. Path possession must not become authority to delete a live lease (#3954). Any change that reverses that doctrine must be stated as an explicit #3954 doctrine change on a separate lean, not as silent first-ship on this issue.
5. Optional adjacent: Codex leave/cleanup that presents the host owner so session:end can clear when the host still publishes identity. That is complementary to README/doctor discovery, not a substitute for it.

issueCommentThread.body:
UAT: **focused-test-pass-1**

`nheroux-bit` cannot apply labels on this repo (`AddLabelsToLabelable` denied). Please add the `focused-test-pass-1` label to this issue.

Adoption blocker.

This is about Swarm: letting an agent, or several agents, carry a piece of work through to a finished pull request. A single person should still have a simple way to run one story.

What a new person hits: A Codex session that was abandoned still holds the "this folder is in use" lock. Ending the session from the command line cannot release it.

Why that ruins the product for them: The project is stuck busy, and the unlock command does not work. They did not do anything wrong. They closed a window.

How likely: Medium-high for Codex users. It happens the moment a session is abandoned, which is normal while poking at a new tool.

model: grok-4.5
```quarantined
role: triage
```

mechanism-shaped: true
design-critique: warranted, because an abandoned Codex session can leave occupancy with host:none / address:none and a normal-shell session:end refuses for missing identity, so the worktree stays locked while the only working recovery (occupancy:release --session-id from occupancy.json) is out-of-band and not first-class in README recovery copy.

charter: refutation
refutation-target: An abandoned Codex session that leaves occupancy with host:none / address:none may keep the worktree locked from a normal shell, because session:end requires a presented session identity and the only recovery is copying occupancy:release --session-id=<id from occupancy.json> as an undocumented out-of-band path.

arc-mode: no-ingest
yolo-standing: yes
spend: N=1
spend-ask: asked

The operator answered with recommended N per issue after the missing-token ask. This is a concrete UAT/occupancy recovery defect on abandoned Codex leases, not a whole-motion babysit hang. Recommended spend N=1.

pain: P1, P2, P3

P1. Abandoned Codex (Ctrl+C leave) can leave occupancy with host:none / address:none, heartbeat == claimed_at, and no recorded write, so the worktree stays locked after the session is gone.
P2. deft session:end from a normal PowerShell with no presented session identity refuses ("This process presented no session identity") and does not clear that lease.
P3. The working recovery is occupancy:release --session-id=<id from occupancy.json>, which is not first-class in README / cold-start recovery copy, so operators rediscover it after setup and after ingest.

Fresh round-1 critic against Stop 1 write-back 5857510383. HEAD at dispatch equals `650ab1a614cd6049b4c70c2b48fa181ffef5455e`. Pin reads via `git show` that SHA. Thread inputs honored at the inclusive ceiling.

## Overstated "only" and "undocumented" recovery
sharpens-framing
Evidence: At the pin, `releaseOccupancy` clears an expired lease without ownership (`occupancy.test.ts` "clears expired residue without ownership (#3604)"); `OCCUPANCY_TTL_MS` is 20 minutes and `liveOccupancyOnTree` treats heartbeat-stale as free for claim-over. Empty-presenter deny text from `formatOccupancyRemediation` already embeds `occupancy:release --session-id=<reported-session-id>` (or the inlined shell-safe id). `content/commands.md` already records the shared identity chain (#3954) and that anonymous release of the occupant recorded in the lease file stays refused. `README.md` at this SHA has no occupancy / `session:end` recovery recipe.
Failure mode: Binding the Stop 1 premise as written steers harvest toward inventing a new unlock verb or reversing anonymous live-release refusal, while operators already have TTL expiry, deny-embedded copy-paste release, and confirmed steal for intentional owner transition.
Disposition: Keep the README / cold-start discoverability gap; drop "only" and "undocumented out-of-band" as absolute claims. Name TTL claim-over and the deny-printed recipe as existing mechanisms before any new surface.

## host:none / address:none are metadata, not the actor
sharpens-framing
Evidence: `occupancyHost` / `occupancyAddress` default to the string `"none"` when env is empty (`occupancy.ts`). The live actor is `record.sessionId`. Empty presentation is `resolvePresentedIdentity` source `"none"` with `sessionId: ""`, which is distinct from those host/address fields. UAT body and Stop 1 lead with host/address none as if that were the lock cause.
Failure mode: A lean scoped to fixing host/address metadata misses the real gate (live `sessionId` plus empty presenter outside a host hook) and can ship cosmetic metadata work while the abandoned-lease UX stays.
Disposition: Reframe the target around abandoned live `sessionId` + normal-shell empty identity; treat host/address none as ordinary unset metadata.

## Anonymous live release is answered-against doctrine
sharpens-framing
Evidence: `occupancy.test.ts` "refuses an anonymous caller the occupant recorded in the lease (#3954)" states the open question was answered against: reading the occupant out of the file and releasing would make path possession into authority to delete a live lease. `commands.md` repeats that anonymous release stays refused. Bare `session:end` / `occupancy:release` with no `--session-id` / `DEFT_SESSION_ID` / host owner against a live lease returns the measured "presented no session identity" denial. Codex-in-host lifecycle rewrite can inject `--session-id` on exact verbs; a normal PowerShell has no host publisher, so empty presentation is expected.
Failure mode: Taking the issue Expected line ("`deft session:end` from a normal shell can clear a stale lease") as the Bound remedy without reconciling #3954 reopens anonymous live release and weakens the cooperative bearer-id boundary under the injection / swarm lens on shared occupancy authority.
Disposition: Scope harvest to first-class operator discovery of the existing explicit `--session-id=<id>` recipe (README / doctor), Codex leave/cleanup that presents the host owner, and honest "wait TTL / claim-over" copy. Reopening anonymous live auto-release needs an explicit #3954 doctrine change, stated as such on the lean.

## Refutation target survival

The target survives in sharpened form: an abandoned Codex conversation can leave a live occupancy lease; a normal-shell bare `session:end` refuses while that lease is live; operators then need an explicit session id; README cold-start does not teach that path. Absolute "only / undocumented out-of-band" recovery claims, and causal host:none / address:none framing, are the sharpening findings above.

## In plain English

An abandoned Codex session can leave a live occupancy lease. A normal PowerShell with no session identity cannot clear that lease with bare session:end, and README cold-start does not teach the working occupancy:release --session-id=<id> recipe. Absolute "only / undocumented" recovery claims overstate the hole: TTL claim-over and deny-printed copy-paste release already exist, and anonymous live release was answered against under #3954. Confirming this map means the Bound remedy list is the build contract. The same parent wrote the Stop 1 warrant and this map. Critic 5857545972 checks the findings. Whether the list covers the three pains stays open until a later critic targets those cites.

**Lean:** the refutation target survives in sharpened form. This map is the bind.

## P2 bare session:end refuse under empty identity
footnote
Evidence: `occupancy.test.ts` "refuses an anonymous caller the occupant recorded in the lease (#3954)" still denies empty presentation with "presented no session identity" and leaves the live lease. `commands.md` keeps anonymous release of the occupant recorded in the lease file refused. Bound remedy items 1 and 4 keep that refuse, teach the explicit `--session-id=<id from occupancy.json>` owner path, and forbid silent reopen of anonymous live auto-release.
Failure mode: Reading the issue Expected line ("`deft session:end` from a normal shell can clear a stale lease") as first-ship would reopen #3954; the lean rejects that reading.
Disposition: Items 1+4 cover P2 as unblockability via documented explicit release, with bare empty-presenter refuse retained. No new unlock verb.

footnote
Evidence: `occupancyHost` / `occupancyAddress` default to the string `"none"` when env is empty; the live actor is `record.sessionId`. `OCCUPANCY_TTL_MS` is 20 minutes; `clears expired residue without ownership (#3604)` remains. Bound remedy items 1-3 reframe the defect onto abandoned live `sessionId` plus normal-shell empty identity, keep TTL claim-over, and make the immediate explicit-release path first-class. Item 5 (Codex leave/cleanup that presents the host owner) is optional complementary, not load-bearing for the cite. Item 2 forbids inventing a new unlock verb whose sole job is abandoned-lease clear.
Failure mode: Treating host/address none as the lock cause, or treating optional item 5 as required first-ship, would mis-scope harvest while the lean already scopes P1 onto discoverable explicit release plus existing TTL.
Disposition: Items 1+2 cover P1 under the accepted round-1 sharpening. Abandoned leases may still form and stay live inside TTL; the relieved pain is operator unlock without rediscovery or anonymous auto-release. Item 5 may reduce abandon formation later; it is not required for this cite.

## Injection / swarm lens (shared occupancy authority)

The target changes cooperative bearer-id release on shared worktree state. Bound remedy item 4 keeps path possession from becoming authority to delete a live lease (#3954). Explicit `--session-id=<id>` is presented identity, distinct from anonymous file-read release. Item 2 keeps TTL / deny-embedded recipe and refuses a greenfield unlock verb. No finding reopens that doctrine.

## Coverage verdict

Under the lean's accepted Takes, Bound remedy items 1-4 cover pain-P1, pain-P2, and pain-P3 without reopening #3954 anonymous live release and without inventing a new unlock verb. Item 5 stays optional adjacent. Footnote-only audit; bind map stays bindable on these cites.
